articles.zh: 亿万富翁为什么在建地堡？
body: Some of the world's richest people are spending millions on underground shelters, and this episode asks a simple question: what exactly are they afraid of?
世界上一些最有钱的人正花几百万建地下庇护所，这期节目问了一个简单的问题：他们到底在怕什么？
The hosts explain that these bunkers can include swimming pools, cinemas and food supplies for years, which sounds more like a luxury hotel than a hiding place.
主持人介绍说，这些地堡里可以有游泳池、电影院和够吃好几年的食物，听起来更像豪华酒店而不是藏身处。
In the end, the discussion turns to ordinary people: instead of preparing for the end of the world, maybe we should work together to make it better.
最后，讨论回到普通人身上：与其为世界末日做准备，不如一起努力让世界变得更好。

articles.en: Should we pay more for chocolate?
articles.zh: 我们该为巧克力多花钱吗？
body: Chocolate prices keep rising, and this episode explains why: bad weather and plant disease have damaged cocoa farms in West Africa, where most of the world's cocoa grows.
巧克力价格一直在涨，这期节目解释了原因：恶劣天气和植物病害破坏了西非的可可农场，而世界上大部分可可都产自那里。
Surprisingly, many cocoa farmers stay poor even when chocolate is expensive, because only a tiny part of the price goes back to them.
令人意外的是，即使巧克力卖得很贵，很多可可农依然贫穷，因为价格里只有很小一部分回到他们手中。
The hosts suggest that paying a little more for fairly traded chocolate could help farmers earn a decent living and protect the future of chocolate itself.
主持人建议，为公平贸易巧克力多付一点钱，既能让农民过上体面生活，也能保住巧克力本身的未来。

articles.zh: 英国人的客套话到底什么意思？
body: British people are famous for not saying what they really mean, and this episode looks at the hidden messages behind everyday polite phrases.
英国人以'不直说心里话'闻名，这期节目研究了日常客套话背后隐藏的真实意思。
For example, when someone says 'not bad', they may actually mean 'very good', and 'interesting' can secretly mean 'I don't like it at all'.
比如有人说 not bad（不差），其实可能是'非常好'；而 interesting（有意思），可能偷偷表示'我一点也不喜欢'。
Learning these unwritten rules helps language learners avoid confusion and understand what British speakers are really thinking behind their smiles.
学会这些不成文的规则，能帮语言学习者少踩坑，听懂英国人微笑背后真正在想什么。

articles.en: Why the rainbow you see is unique to you
articles.zh: 为什么你看到的彩虹独一无二？
body: This story shares a lovely science fact: no two people ever see exactly the same rainbow, because it depends on where each person is standing.
这个故事分享了一个可爱的科学事实：没有两个人能看到完全相同的彩虹，因为彩虹取决于每个人站的位置。
A rainbow is made when sunlight passes through raindrops and splits into different colours, so the light reaching your eyes follows its own special path.
彩虹是阳光穿过雨滴、分解成不同颜色形成的，所以到达你眼睛的光走的是一条专属路线。
In other words, the rainbow you admire belongs only to you – a nice reminder that everyone sees the world a little differently.
换句话说，你欣赏的那道彩虹只属于你——这也温柔地提醒我们：每个人看世界的角度都不太一样。

articles.en: How unhygienic is it to wear your shoes at home?
articles.zh: 在家穿鞋到底有多不卫生？
body: Do you take your shoes off at the door? This story looks at what scientists found on the bottom of everyday shoes – and it is not pretty.
你进门会脱鞋吗？这个故事讲了科学家在日常鞋底上发现的东西——画面不太美好。
Research shows shoes can carry bacteria from streets, toilets and soil into our homes, spreading germs onto clean floors and carpets.
研究显示，鞋子会把街道、厕所和泥土里的细菌带进家里，把病菌传到干净的地板和地毯上。
The good news is simple: leaving shoes at the door, a habit common in many Asian homes, is one of the easiest ways to keep your home healthier.
好消息很简单：把鞋留在门口——很多亚洲家庭的老习惯——就是让家更健康的最简单方法之一。
